newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank Canada posts record quarterly profit.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank Canada posts record quarterly profit.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada, Canada's biggest bank, said Wednesday second-quarter profit rose to a record C$403 million ($291 million), or C$1.20 (87 cents) a share, in line with analysts' expectations.

"This quarter was marked by strong growth in revenues from wealth management (mutual fund, brokerage, investment management and custody) and other fee-based businesses, solid loan growth and better asset quality," Royal Bank Chief Executive John Cleghorn said in a statement.
"Looking forward to the rest of 1997, we continue to expect good performances in the areas of revenue growth, efficiency and asset quality," Cleghorn added.
The bank earned C$340 million ($245 million), or C97 cents (70 cents) a share, in the year earlier period.
Royal Bank said its provision for credit losses in the second quarter fell 14 percent to C$95 million ($69 million) from C$110 million ($79.5 million) in the previous year.
Net impaired loans fell C$67 million ($48.4 million) to C$220 million ($159 million) from last quarter.
Assets increased C$40.9 billion ($29.5 billion) or 20 percent to C$250.8 billion ($181.2 billion) at April 30, 1997.
For the first six months, Royal Bank's earnings rose to C$802 million ($577 million) or C$2.38 ($1.71) a share from year earlier C$696 million ($501 million) or C$1.98 ($1.43) a share.
Royal Bank stock fell C10 cents to C$60.80 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday in tandem with other banking shares.
